target_customer: New parents with iPhones who pay a subscription to organize baby photos
problem: Parents take thousands of baby photos and never sort or share them. The app uses AI to pick the best photos and build stories and albums.
business_model: Consumer subscription (4.99 dollars per month or 39.99 per year in 2018), no ads

founders.name: Chris Lau
previous_startups: Consumer apps built with brother Daniel Lau over several years (names not given)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he and his wife had a baby while the brothers were brainstorming ideas.

founders.name: Daniel Lau
previous_startups: Consumer apps built with brother Chris Lau over several years (names not given)

competitors.name: Lifecake
competitors.what: Visual timeline app for baby photos

competitors.name: Tinybeans
competitors.what: Private photo sharing app for parents

competitors.name: BlinkPix
competitors.what: Makes it easier to print and mail photos

technical_complexity.rationale: On-device image selection and curation for baby photos using AI, with story and album generation. Standard mobile engineering with an ML component in 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Photo curation features are copyable by platform photo apps. Subscription revenue gave some stickiness but no network effects were stated.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch compared the product to memory-resurfacing features in Timehop, Facebook Memories and Momento. No source shows an acquisition; the app is still listed in app stores with a 2026 copyright.

market_need_then: In March 2018 TechCrunch reported about 54,000 paying users, up from about 2,000 at launch 16 months earlier, which shows paying demand among parents.

branding.domain_note: Company site uses preciousapp.com with web version at precious.app; purchase history not found.

identity.visual_style: Warm baby-themed app store imagery with photo art, stickers and frames

rebrands.why: Not stated. TechCrunch says the app launched as Baby Art 16 months earlier; the App Store listing still shows Baby Art subscription names.

brand_strength.rationale: A warm but generic name and no evidence of press about the brand or community beyond app reviews.

outcome_analysis: Precious is a small, self-funded consumer subscription app that had 54,000 paying users at the time of Demo Day in 2018 and is still operating under Curious Creators Co. with a Feb 2026 Android release. No venture round or exit is confirmed, so the story is steady bootstrapped operation rather than a venture-scale outcome.
notes: TechCrunch (2018-03-27) says the company was self-funded apart from YC. An aggregator (Seedtable/Bounce Watch) lists a 1.0 million dollar seed in April 2018 and 120 thousand pre-seed in Jan 2018, with Collaborative Fund, FundersClub, Sesame Street and Locus Ventures; seen only on aggregators, unverified, so not recorded as rounds. Website copyright holder is Curious Creators Co. App Store release date given as 2016-04-21.
